question: Which of the following statements is **NOT **correct about alluvial soil?

options.text: Old alluvial is called ‘bangar’ and new alluvial is called ‘khadar’.
Deltas of Mahanadi, the Godavari and the Krishna are made from alluvial soil
Northern plains are made of alluvial soil
In the Himalayan region we find alluvial soil.

solution:
The correct answer is **__In the Himalayan region we find alluvial soil.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil is not found In the Himalayan region.**
 
• **Alluvial soils:**
 
 
• These soils are called** transported soil** because although they are formed near the water bodies, these soils get transported from their origin to several other places by various natural agents, especially by gravity.
 
• The alluvial soil is made up of particles like **silt, sand, and clay and has an adequate amount of phosphoric acid, potash, and lime.**
 
• It is of two types:
 
 
• The older alluvial soil is known as **Bhangar.**
 
• The newer alluvial soil is known as** Khadar.**
 
 
 
• The alluvial soil covers a total of** 40%** of the land.
 
• These soils are found in the **northern plains beginning from Punjab to West Bengal and Assam.**
 
• It is also** found in deltas of rivers like Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri, and Mahanadi in peninsular India.**
 
• The** main crops **cultivated are wheat, rice, maize, sugarcane, pulses, and oilseeds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• On the basis of **genesis, color, composition, and location,** the soils of India have been classified into:

 
 
• (1) Alluvial soils (ii) Black soils (iii) Red and Yellow soils (iv) Laterite soils (V) Arid soils (vi) Saline soils (vii) Peaty soils (viii) Forest soils.
 
 
 
• On the** basis of the size of the particles **that make up a soil defines its gardening characteristics:
 
 
• (1) Clay soil (ii) Silty soil (iii) Sandy soil (iv) Stones (v) Chalky soils
 
 
 
• **Saline soil:**
 
 
• It refers to Arid soil.
 
• These are derived from the disintegration of adjacent rocks and are largely blown from coastal regions and the Indus valley.
 
• They are developed in western Rajasthan. Due to the dry climate, high temperature and accelerated evaporation, they lack moisture and humus.
 
 
 
• **Calcerous soil:**
 
 
• They are also known as chalky soils.
 
• These soils contain calcium carbonate or lime.
 
• They are very alkaline and may be light or heavy.
